title: Quarterly mosaic briefing and staff chores
content:
Purpose
-------
This is a working brief for the upcoming quarter: consolidated narrative for the exec update, a draft set of company-level OKRs, and a pragmatic all-hands flow with breakout chores for each hub. The language here is deliberately conversational and action-focused — use this to rehearse, iterate, and hand off to comms.

Audience
--------
Primary: Exec team, product-ops, heads of eng, SRE, and go-to-market. Secondary: broader leadership who will present at the all-hands or run breakouts.

High-level narrative (2–3 lines we want people to remember)
------------------------------------------------------
- We shipped baseline reliability and a set of cost controls that reduced per-token spend by ~18% in pilot accounts.
- This quarter we go from "cost wins" to "platform wins": predictable SLAs for Dedicated, routable private deployments, and a rollout blueprint for customers eager to migrate from experimental to production.

Top-line talking points for the exec update (3–5 bullets)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Progress vs last quarter: Hosting throughput +40% peak, median latency down 18ms on production workloads; Dedicated beta closed 3 pilot contracts (estimated ARR $1.2M).
- Risks to call out: supply-side GPU scarcity in APAC window, three models show quality drift vs upstream checkpoints (we have eval jobs queued).
- Commitment for next quarter: two enterprise sales commitments, 99.95% ded. availability SLA baseline, and a public evaluative report showing performance/cost per model class.

Draft company-level OKRs (proposal — keep it tight)
------------------------------------------------
OKR 1 — Production Reliability & SLAs
- Objective: Make inference predictable at customer scale.
- Key results (KR):
  - KR1.1: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pools across EMEA + NAM (measured at route-level)
  - KR1.2: Reduce P95 tail latency by 15% for hosted API gen endpoints (seq len 512)
  - KR1.3: Deploy automated fallback policies for top 10 customers with a <5% incident escalation rate

OKR 2 — Unit economics for high-throughput applications
- Objective: Drive down per-token cost without degrading quality.
- KRs:
  - KR2.1: 20% reduction in average cost/token for top-20 accounts (workload-weighted)
  - KR2.2: Publish and ship at least 2 quantization profiles with verified quality bounds (measured via evaluation suite)
  - KR2.3: Launch an Optimize quick-start (templates + one-click profiles) used by 50 customers

OKR 3 — Enterprise motion and private deployments
- Objective: Make Private deployments straightforward for compliance-sensitive customers.
- KRs:
  - KR3.1: Close 4 Private pilot contracts with revenue > $600k ARR committed
  - KR3.2: Release V1 of private control plane install/runbook with <3 customer blockers in pilot
  - KR3.3: KMS/HSM integration documented and tested by 2 customers

OKR 4 — Developer experience and platform adoption
- Objective: Reduce time-to-first-success for engineering teams using Redwood.
- KRs:
  - KR4.1: Reduce median time from signup -> first successful inference to <1 day
  - KR4.2: Increase SDK adoption: 40% of playbooks use SDK vs raw REST
  - KR4.3: Ship two example reference apps that show cost/latency tradeoffs for common patterns

Notes on metrics and measurement
-------------------------------
- Ownership: Each KR should be owned by a single leader (we'll assign next week). Measurement windows must be instrumented in Console (per-route dashboards) and backed by sampled traces.
- Tolerance: KRs should have an "amber" tolerance band for external supply shocks (e.g., GPU capacity) — we will annotate any misses with causality in the weekly radar.

All-hands structure (60–75 minutes)
----------------------------------
1) 00:00–00:05 — Welcome (CEO) — two high-level signals, one headline metric, and a single ask (what we want from the company this quarter).
2) 00:05–00:12 — Product momentum montage (30s clips / bullet points) — biggest wins vs last quarter (eng lead).
3) 00:12–00:22 — Customer spotlight (Solutions) — trio of quick wins from pilot customers and lessons.
4) 00:22–00:35 — Exec update + new company OKRs (CEO + product) — show the proposed OKRs, why they matter, and how they connect to team charters.
5) 00:35–00:50 — Breakouts (voluntary) — three simultaneous hubs: Reliability & SRE, GTM + Dedicated, Developer Experience + Onboarding. Each breakout has a 6-minute micro-agenda and a single artifact to return (a 1-slide summary).
6) 00:50–00:65 — Report back and final asks (panel of breakout leads) — capture 3 concrete commitments from each hub.
7) 00:65–00:75 — Closing and Q&A (CEO + product) — address 3 pre-collected hard questions, then live Qs for 5 minutes.

Breakout chore list (who does what — lightweight)
------------------------------------------------
Reliability & SRE hub (lead: Samir Rao)
- Prework: bring 2 short postmortems with remediation timelines (Samir).
- In-session: prioritize top-3 infra bets (KV cache, routing fallback, autoscaler).
- Deliverable: single slide with prioritized bets + owners + 30/60/90 plan.

GTM + Dedicated (lead: Maya Patel)
- Prework: mini case study from pilot contract (sales + solutions).
- In-session: identify 2 obstacles to faster contract expansion.
- Deliverable: slide with 2 proposed mechanics (pricing tweak, pilot success checklist).

Developer Experience + Onboarding (lead: Jordan Alvarez)
- Prework: capture 3 friction points from new accounts in last 90 days.
- In-session: rapid ideation on 1-click start flows and error messaging changes.
- Deliverable: slide with one immediate small experiment to reduce TTF (time-to-first-success).

Rehearsal checklist (week prior and 48 hours prior)
--------------------------------------------------
- Week prior: finalize slides for CEO and product (Avery), collect 6-sentence customer quotes (Solutions), and reserve breakout facilitators.
- 72 hours: run a dry run with execs (12–15 minutes) — check AV, captions, and slide timings (Avery + ops).
- 24 hours: publish "what to expect" note to company (Maya) with breakout sign-up links and prework.
- 2 hours pre: slack reminders for leads and a final systems check (ops).

Fallbacks and escalation trees
----------------------------
- If CEO unavailable: product lead runs main deck and the head of GTM covers customer spotlight.
- If a live demo fails: fallback to pre-recorded clip; backup slides with screenshots and logs.
- If breakout leads no-show: a predetermined alternate facilitator takes each hub (list in Confluence linked artifact).

Risks and mitigations (top 5)
-----------------------------
1) GPU capacity in APAC: escalate to infra procurement and surface a soft quota for large pilots.
2) Model quality regressions: freeze model rollouts, run diag eval suite, and block auto-rollout until checks pass.
3) Sales churn due to integration friction: offer a "white-glove" two-week concierge onboarding for at-risk pilots.
4) Console metric gaps: add one prioritized dashboard with per-route cost and latency for top 30 customers.
5) Communication noise: centralize questions on a single thread and post weekly highlights to reduce redundant asks.

Open questions (to resolve by next leadership sync)
------------------------------------------------
- Who owns the final sign-off on company-level OKRs? Proposed: CEO + Head of Product.
- Do we keep four company OKRs or condense to three? Tradeoffs: focus vs coverage.
- Which quantization profiles are prioritized for the public release? (Applied ML to propose top-2).

Immediate action items (next 10 days)
------------------------------------
- Avery: finalize all-hands script and share editable deck (due 2025-03-05).
- Maya: draft "what to expect" note and breakout sign-up page (due 2025-03-06).
- Samir: collect infra postmortems and proposed bets slide (due 2025-03-06).
- Jordan: assemble onboarding friction list and reference apps status (due 2025-03-07).
- Priya: schedule rehearsal and confirm AV test slot (due 2025-03-07).

Notes to self / iteration log
---------------------------
- 2025-02-15: initial draft — focus on clarity and short asks; pulled metrics from weekly radar.
- 2025-02-20: added Dedicated revenue targets after sales sync.
- 2025-02-28: tightened KR language to be measurable; added baseline tolerance clause.
- 2025-03-02: updated rehearsal plan per ops availability and added fallback demo plan.

Appendix (quick references)
--------------------------
- Shortlist of customers to invite to spotlight: PilotCo, RetailAI, DocStream (ask Solutions for approvals).
- Link to evaluation suite and thresholds: see linked artifacts for Confluence ID.
- One-line elevator pitches for each OKR to use on slides:
  - Reliability: "Customers can rely on us at any scale."
  - Economics: "Better inference at a lower unit cost."
  - Private: "Private deployments without ops friction."
  - Developer experience: "Get an LLM feature into prod in a day."

End of draft — please add inline comments in this doc rather than separate threads so we can keep iteration centralized.
